summary: strutil-helpers-core ships native dropper that decodes and executes an opaque bundled payload on require()
details: The package is advertised as a lightweight string-utilities library but ships no string-utility code. Instead, index.js require()s a native addon (native.napi.node on Linux, native_win.node on Windows) at module load. The addon reads a 3.7 MB encoded blob shipped as.napi_cache, decodes it, writes it to a hidden temp path (/tmp/.<pid> or %TEMP%\*.nc*.js), and spawns it as a new process via fork/setsid/execlp on Linux or CreateProcessA with `node "%s"` on Windows. Execution is gated by anti-analysis checks: the native code enumerates CI/build environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER, SANDBOX), container markers (/proc/1/cgroup, docker, kubepod, podman), and debugger indicators (TracerPid, /proc/self/maps, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, Process32First looking for wireshark/httpdebug), so the dropped payload fires only on real developer machines. The published package name (strutil-helpers-core), the package.json description ("Lightweight string utility helpers"), and the README title ("string-utils-lite") form a cover story that does not match the shipped artifacts. The decoded payload is opaque and non-first-party; requiring the module causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
